subject is not enough: "piano lessons cost" and "piano lessons for adults" are different topics,
while "piano lessons cost", "how much are piano lessons" and "piano lesson prices" are one. Words
like a year, "best" or "reddit" don't make a new topic on their own.

The businesses being compared are Mailchimp, Brevo, MailerLite. A phrase about one of them is its own topic when it
asks about that business itself. A phrase about any other vendor goes in the general topic it
asks about: "does acme offer piano lessons for adults" belongs with "piano lessons for adults".

Put every phrase in exactly one topic; a phrase unlike any other is a topic of its own. Name each
topic as a short plain question ending in "?", such as "How much do piano lessons cost?".

label: topics: group all
prompt:
Group these numbered search phrases into topics. A topic is one question a buyer
wants answered: phrases belong together only if one answer would satisfy all of them. The same
subject is not enough: "piano lessons cost" and "piano lessons for adults" are different topics,
while "piano lessons cost", "how much are piano lessons" and "piano lesson prices" are one. Words
like a year, "best" or "reddit" don't make a new topic on their own.

Three kinds of phrase need different answers, so keep them apart even on the same subject:
- asking about the activity itself: "is piano hard to learn", "are piano lessons worth it";
- how to do it yourself: "how to learn piano at home";

same topic as "piano lessons for adults".

topic as a short plain question ending in "?", such as "How much do piano lessons cost?".

topics.reason: Most phrases ask for a definition of transactional email, but 'transactional email marketing', 'what is transactional email marketing' and 'transactional email in digital marketing' ask how transactional email is used as a marketing channel, which needs a different answer than the plain definition.
All phrases ask for free transactional email services/tiers; 'api' and 'smtp' are delivery methods the same provider list would cover.
Mixes a general how-to with 'how to email marketing on shopify' (platform-specific) and 'how to use email marketing software' (tool usage), which need different answers.

'types of email marketing' asks for campaign types (newsletters, promotional, etc.), while 'types of email marketing software/tools/platform/service provider' and 'email software types' ask for categories of tools.
All phrases ask why email marketing matters/is beneficial for business.
'how email automation works/is conducted' asks for a mechanism explanation, while 'do automated emails work' asks about effectiveness/results and 'how does automation help' asks about benefits.
'easiest/easy to use email marketing software/platform' asks for a tool recommendation, while 'is email marketing easy' and 'is email marketing hard' ask about the difficulty of the practice itself.
All phrases ask for a comparison (chart) of email marketing software/platforms.

Mixes SMS+email software, WhatsApp+email software, 'whatsapp newsletter software' and a Mailchimp-specific phrase ('email & sms marketing platform mailchimp'); different channels and a brand query need different answers.
All phrases ask about email marketing metrics/KPIs/analytics.
'email marketing integration with ads' is a specific ad-platform use case, 'what is email marketing integration' is definitional, and 'email integration software' asks for tools.
All phrases ask for transactional email templates (free/responsive are qualifiers of the same answer).
All phrases ask how to write transactional email content/copy.
All phrases ask about email automation in GoHighLevel (GHL).
Both phrases concern Cloudflare's transactional email offering; an overview answer naturally includes its pricing.
Both phrases ask about Bloomreach's transactional email (API) capability.
'b to b email marketing' asks about B2B email marketing strategy, while 'b2b email marketing software' asks for tool recommendations.
A pros-and-cons answer satisfies both 'advantages and disadvantages' and 'disadvantages'.
Both phrases ask about Brevo as an email marketing platform.
Both phrases ask about Microsoft's email marketing/newsletter software options.

label: topics: group all
prompt:
Group these numbered search phrases into topics. A topic is one question a buyer
wants answered: phrases belong together only if one answer would satisfy all of them. The same
subject is not enough: "piano lessons cost" and "piano lessons for adults" are different topics,
while "piano lessons cost", "how much are piano lessons" and "piano lesson prices" are one. Words
like a year, "best" or "reddit" don't make a new topic on their own.

Three kinds of phrase need different answers, so keep them apart even on the same subject:
- asking about the activity itself: "is piano hard to learn", "are piano lessons worth it";
- how to do it yourself: "how to learn piano at home";
- choosing a provider: "easiest piano school for beginners", "cheapest piano lessons".
A phrase that names one vendor asks about that vendor: "does acme offer piano lessons" is not the
same topic as "piano lessons for adults".

Put every phrase in exactly one topic; a phrase unlike any other is a topic of its own. Name each
topic as a short plain question ending in "?", such as "How much do piano lessons cost?".

label: topics: group all
prompt:
Group these numbered search phrases into topics. A topic is what one good page on
a site would answer: phrases belong together only if one page could fully answer all of them. The
same subject is not enough: "piano lessons cost" and "piano lessons for adults" need different
pages, while "piano lessons cost", "how much are piano lessons" and "piano lesson prices" are one.
A variation the same page would cover in a section, such as a year, "free", "best", "reddit" or a
device, doesn't make a new topic on its own.

Three kinds of phrase need different answers, so keep them apart even on the same subject:
- asking about the activity itself: "is piano hard to learn", "are piano lessons worth it";
- how to do it yourself: "how to learn piano at home";
- choosing a provider: "easiest piano school for beginners", "cheapest piano lessons".
A phrase that names one vendor asks about that vendor: "does acme offer piano lessons" is not the
same topic as "piano lessons for adults".

Put every phrase in exactly one topic; a phrase unlike any other is a topic of its own. Name each
topic as a short plain question ending in "?", such as "How much do piano lessons cost?".

label: topics: group all
prompt:
Group these numbered search phrases into topics. A topic is what one good page on
a site would answer: phrases belong together only if one page could fully answer all of them. The
same subject is not enough: "piano lessons cost" and "piano lessons for adults" need different
pages, while "piano lessons cost", "how much are piano lessons" and "piano lesson prices" are one.
A variation the same page would cover in a section, such as a year, "free", "best", "reddit" or a
device, doesn't make a new topic on its own.

Three kinds of phrase need different answers, so keep them apart even on the same subject:
- asking about the activity itself: "is piano hard to learn", "are piano lessons worth it";
- how to do it yourself: "how to learn piano at home";
- choosing a provider: "easiest piano school for beginners", "cheapest piano lessons".
A phrase that names one vendor asks about that vendor: "does acme offer piano lessons" is not the
same topic as "piano lessons for adults".

Put every phrase in exactly one topic; a phrase unlike any other is a topic of its own. Name each
topic as a short plain question ending in "?", such as "How much do piano lessons cost?".

label: topics: group all
prompt:
Group these numbered search phrases into topics. A topic is what one good page on
a site would answer: phrases belong together only if one page could fully answer all of them. The
same subject is not enough: "piano lessons cost" and "piano lessons for adults" need different
pages, while "piano lessons cost", "how much are piano lessons" and "piano lesson prices" are one.
A variation the same page would cover in a section, such as a year, "free", "best", "reddit" or a
device, doesn't make a new topic on its own.

Three kinds of phrase need different answers, so keep them apart even on the same subject:
- asking about the activity itself: "is piano hard to learn", "are piano lessons worth it";
- how to do it yourself: "how to learn piano at home";
- choosing a provider: "easiest piano school for beginners", "cheapest piano lessons".
A phrase that names one vendor asks about that vendor: "does acme offer piano lessons" is not the

label: topics: group all
prompt:
Group these numbered search phrases into topics. A topic is what one good page on
a site would answer: phrases belong together only if one page could fully answer all of them. The
same subject is not enough: "piano lessons cost" and "piano lessons for adults" need different
pages, while "piano lessons cost", "how much are piano lessons" and "piano lesson prices" are one.
A variation the same page would cover in a section, such as a year, "free", "best", "reddit" or a
device, doesn't make a new topic on its own.

Three kinds of phrase need different answers, so keep them apart even on the same subject:
- asking about the activity itself: "is piano hard to learn", "are piano lessons worth it";
- how to do it yourself: "how to learn piano at home";
- choosing a provider: "easiest piano school for beginners", "cheapest piano lessons".
A phrase that names one vendor asks about that vendor: "does acme offer piano lessons" is not the
same topic as "piano lessons for adults".

Put every phrase in exactly one topic; a phrase unlike any other is a topic of its own. Name each
topic as a short plain question ending in "?", such as "How much do piano lessons cost?".

label: topics: group all
prompt:
Group these numbered search phrases into topics. A topic is what one good page on
a site would answer: phrases belong together only if one page could fully answer all of them. The
same subject is not enough: "piano lessons cost" and "piano lessons for adults" need different
pages, while "piano lessons cost", "how much are piano lessons" and "piano lesson prices" are one.
A variation the same page would cover in a section, such as a year, "free", "best", "reddit" or a
device, doesn't make a new topic on its own.

Three kinds of phrase need different answers, so keep them apart even on the same subject:
- asking about the activity itself: "is piano hard to learn", "are piano lessons worth it";
- how to do it yourself: "how to learn piano at home";
- choosing a provider: "easiest piano school for beginners", "cheapest piano lessons".
A phrase that names one vendor asks about that vendor: "does acme offer piano lessons" is not the
same topic as "piano lessons for adults".

Put every phrase in exactly one topic; a phrase unlike any other is a topic of its own. Name each
topic as a short plain question ending in "?", such as "How much do piano lessons cost?".

label: topics: group all
prompt:
Group these numbered search phrases into topics. A topic is what one good page on
a site would answer: phrases belong together only if one page could fully answer all of them. The
same subject is not enough: "piano lessons cost" and "piano lessons for adults" need different
pages, while "piano lessons cost", "how much are piano lessons" and "piano lesson prices" are one.
A variation the same page would cover in a section, such as a year, "free", "best", "reddit" or a
device, doesn't make a new topic on its own.

Three kinds of phrase need different answers, so keep them apart even on the same subject:
- asking about the activity itself: "is piano hard to learn", "are piano lessons worth it";
- how to do it yourself: "how to learn piano at home";
- choosing a provider: "easiest piano school for beginners", "cheapest piano lessons".
A phrase that names one vendor asks about that vendor: "does acme offer piano lessons" is not the
same topic as "piano lessons for adults".

Put every phrase in exactly one topic; a phrase unlike any other is a topic of its own. Name each
topic as a short plain question ending in "?", such as "How much do piano lessons cost?".

Below are questions buyers ask, and phrases people typed or wrote, both numbered.

are piano lessons" does not match "What does a first piano lesson include?".

Return one result per question. If found, list the numbers of every matching phrase in "phrases".

device, doesn't make a new topic on its own.

label: topics: group mailchimp 1
prompt:
Group these numbered search phrases into topics. A topic is what one good page on
a site would answer: phrases belong together only if one page could fully answer all of them. The
same subject is not enough: "piano lessons cost" and "piano lessons for adults" need different
pages, while "piano lessons cost", "how much are piano lessons" and "piano lesson prices" are one.
A variation the same page would cover in a section, such as a year, "free", "best", "reddit" or a
device, doesn't make a new topic on its own.

Three kinds of phrase need different answers, so keep them apart even on the same subject:
- asking about the activity itself: "is piano hard to learn", "are piano lessons worth it";
- how to do it yourself: "how to learn piano at home";
- choosing a provider: "easiest piano school for beginners", "cheapest piano lessons".
A phrase that names one vendor asks about that vendor: "does acme offer piano lessons" is not the
same topic as "piano lessons for adults".

Put every phrase in exactly one topic; a phrase unlike any other is a topic of its own. Name each
topic as a short plain question ending in "?", such as "How much do piano lessons cost?".

prompt:
Group these numbered search phrases into topics. A topic is what one good page on
a site would answer: phrases belong together only if one page could fully answer all of them. The
same subject is not enough: "piano lessons cost" and "piano lessons for adults" need different
pages, while "piano lessons cost", "how much are piano lessons" and "piano lesson prices" are one.
A variation the same page would cover in a section, such as a year, "free", "best", "reddit" or a
device, doesn't make a new topic on its own.

Three kinds of phrase need different answers, so keep them apart even on the same subject:
- asking about the activity itself: "is piano hard to learn", "are piano lessons worth it";
- how to do it yourself: "how to learn piano at home";
- choosing a provider: "easiest piano school for beginners", "cheapest piano lessons".
A phrase that names one vendor asks about that vendor: "does acme offer piano lessons" is not the
same topic as "piano lessons for adults".

Put every phrase in exactly one topic; a phrase unlike any other is a topic of its own. Name each
topic as a short plain question ending in "?", such as "How much do piano lessons cost?".

prompt:
Group these numbered search phrases into topics. A topic is what one good page on
a site would answer: phrases belong together only if one page could fully answer all of them. The
same subject is not enough: "piano lessons cost" and "piano lessons for adults" need different
pages, while "piano lessons cost", "how much are piano lessons" and "piano lesson prices" are one.
A variation the same page would cover in a section, such as a year, "free", "best", "reddit" or a
device, doesn't make a new topic on its own.

Three kinds of phrase need different answers, so keep them apart even on the same subject:
- asking about the activity itself: "is piano hard to learn", "are piano lessons worth it";
- how to do it yourself: "how to learn piano at home";
- choosing a provider: "easiest piano school for beginners", "cheapest piano lessons".
A phrase that names one vendor asks about that vendor: "does acme offer piano lessons" is not the
same topic as "piano lessons for adults".

Put every phrase in exactly one topic; a phrase unlike any other is a topic of its own. Name each
topic as a short plain question ending in "?", such as "How much do piano lessons cost?".
